punchline: Wright says the mind that jumps at every rustle in the bushes was built to get genes along, not to keep you content.
thirty_sec: Robert Wright argues natural selection built the mind to crave, not to be content. A rustle on a hike makes you flinch, even with no snake, because a false alarm beats a missed one. Satisfaction fades so animals keep pursuing food and sex, and speech anxiety is an old alarm in a new place. Meditation lets you watch the feeling before you obey it.
